text.p: Following are some of the leading stories of Norwegian papers this morning:

- Norwegian insurer Vesta may take court action against a possible merger between Aker og RGI. The purpose is to secure Vesta's demand for compensation after the Sleipner rig sank in Gandsfjorden in 1991.

- Consultant and auditing company Coopers & Lybrand is expanding in Norway. During the last 20 months the company has appointed 120 new employees. Coopers & Lybrand is expecting a total growth of 10 percent the next couple of years.

- Family and Children Minister Grete Berget had to answer tough questions from members of parliament at an open hearing. The hearing is on the scandal of youth organisations receiving more financial support from the government than they were entitled to. Grete Berget was herself in a leading position in the Labour Party's youth league when it reported an artificially high number of members and recieved more money than it was entitled to.

- Rema, one of the biggest grocery chains in Norway, is now on the Internet. Customers can order groceries on the net but must still fetch the groceries and pay in the shop. During 1997 customers will be able to pay via Internet and the groceries will be brought to their homes.
- Finance Minister Sigbjoern Johnsen wants to simplify the regulations on taxation for gains on sales of shares. Johnsen wants a lower tax for long-term shareholders than for short-term shareholders.
